exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $76,921.00 as of 2026-11-03 12:01:57 UTC, +0.01% over one hour and -1.15% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $76,303.00 to $78,120.00; spot sits at 34% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -3.56% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($76,980.20) is below the 72-hour average ($77,574.04). Spot is 5.84% below the seven-day high of $81,691.75 and 0.81% above the seven-day low of $76,303.00.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 1.90% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 53.9, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $27.26 billion, equal to 1.76% of the $1.55 trillion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 26 ("Fear"), versus 48 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink BTC/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $77,041.15, 30 minutes before the spot quote and +0.16% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of BTC is anchored near the lower‑half of its 24‑hour range, sitting at 34% of that band (Ex. B), indicating that the market has ample room to rebound toward the midpoint of $77,211, a move supported by the modest 0.01% hour‑over‑hour gain (Ex. A).  

2. Volatility is low at 1.90% daily (Ex. D) while the RSI sits at a neutral 53.9, suggesting the price can climb without triggering over‑extension, and the recent 27.26 billion dollars of volume (Ex. E) provides the liquidity needed for a sustained upward move.  

3. Market sentiment is in “Fear” territory at 26 on the Fear & Greed Index (Ex. F), a classic contrarian signal that the next 24‑hour session will see buyers step in, and the Chainlink feed, trading 0.16% above spot (Ex. G), offers a slightly higher entry point for the Bull.  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The market is entrenched in a short‑term downtrend: BTC has slipped 3.56% over the past seven days, with the 24‑hour average ($76,980.20) below the 72‑hour average ($77,574.04) and trading 5.84% beneath the seven‑day high of $81,691.75 [Ex. C]; this negative momentum predicts further pressure toward the lower bound of the 24‑hour range.  

2. Liquidity remains ample yet indifferent, as $27.26 billion traded in the last 24 hours represents only 1.76% of market cap, providing sufficient depth for a short swing without triggering a liquidity crunch [Ex. E]; combined with a modest realized volatility of 1.90% per day, a short position can capture incremental declines without excessive slippage [Ex. D].  

3. Sentiment is markedly bearish: the Fear & Greed Index sits at 26, down from 48 a week ago, signaling heightened fear and a propensity for further price concessions [Ex. F]; the Chainlink feed, the settlement benchmark, is already 0.16% above spot, offering a slight upward bias for short entry [Ex. G].  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s “short‑term downtrend” claim ignores the neutral momentum shown by the 14‑hour RSI of 53.9, which suggests no decisive bearish pressure [Ex. D]. Moreover, the 24‑hour price sits at only 34 % of its daily range, indicating that the market is near the lower bound and lacks headroom for further decline [Ex. B]. The Bear also overstates “ample liquidity”; $27.26 billion represents merely 1.76 % of market cap, a thin slice that could magnify price impact on any sizable short trade, especially given the modest 1.90 % daily volatility that limits profit potential [Ex. E, D]. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s “room to rebound” argument collapses on the 24‑hour range data: spot sits at the lower‑bound (34% of range) and the seven‑day trend is –3.56% with the 24‑hour average already below the 72‑hour average, indicating persistent down‑pressure, not a latent climb (Ex. B, C). Second, the so‑called “neutral” RSI at 53.9 is meaningless amid a Fear index of 26, which signals deep market anxiety rather than contrarian optimism; fear‑driven selling typically precedes further declines, not rebounds (Ex. D, F). Moreover, the Chainlink feed is merely 0.16% above spot and cannot offset these bearish fundamentals. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds a short position is warranted

findings.finding: Spot price is marginally up hour‑over‑hour but down 1.15% over 24 h, indicating recent weakness
Seven‑day price is –3.56% with the 24‑h average below the 72‑h average, showing bearish momentum
Current price sits at 34% of the 24‑h range, near the lower bound, limiting upside potential
Fear & Greed Index at 26 (Fear) reflects heightened bearish sentiment

ruling.opinion: The exhibits show BTC trading near the low end of its daily band, a recent 3.56% seven‑day decline and a 24‑hour average beneath the three‑day average, all pointing to continued downside pressure. Neutral RSI does not offset the strong bearish bias indicated by the Fear index and range position. Consequently, a short practice position aligns with the prevailing evidence.
ruling.dissent: Bull counsel cites neutral RSI and modest hour‑over‑hour gain, but these factors are outweighed by the clear multi‑day downtrend, low range position, and fear‑driven sentiment.
